What it is: On first setup, old agent files, commands, rules and plan files that SAF did not write move into docs/archive/pre-saf; nothing is deleted.
Good for: A clean SAF layout with no old plan or agent files mixed in, and the old ones kept as history.
Cost: Whatever read the old files in place no longer finds them; move one back by hand if you still need it.
Pick it when: the project already has agent docs or a plan from before SAF.
What it is: Old agent files, commands, rules and plan files stay where they are; files SAF writes still replace same-named ones, with the old copy archived first.
Good for: Your existing agents and commands keep working in place.
Cost: Old plan files stay where the plan check reads them and may raise problems; old agents sit beside SAF's.
Pick it when: you want to keep your existing agent files in place and will merge them yourself.
What it is: Setup ends with a local git commit of the generated files; nothing is pushed.
Good for: The first card can start at once, since it compares changed files against that commit; setup stays one commit you can review.
Cost: The generated files enter your history before you have read them.
Pick it when: you are happy to read the output afterwards and want the card loop to work right away.
What it is: The generated files stay uncommitted and you commit them yourself before the first card.
Good for: You can read or edit the generated files first and choose your own commit message and split.
Cost: task:start refuses in a repo with no commit at all, and a lane start refuses uncommitted plan files.
Pick it when: you want to read the output before it enters history, or commits must follow your own rules.
